samuel2.14.p1.b1.text: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.

samuel2.14.p1.b2.text: “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.”

samuel2.14.p1.b3.text: And Joab put the words in her mouth.

samuel2.14.p2.b2.text: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.

samuel2.14.p2.b3.text: “So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”

samuel2.14.p2.b4.text: “Go home, … and I will give orders on your behalf.”

samuel2.14.p3.b1.text: “May the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!”

samuel2.14.p3.b2.text: “As surely as the LORD lives, … not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”

samuel2.14.p3.b3.text: “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?”

samuel2.14.p3.b4.text: “When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?”

samuel2.14.p4.b1.text: “For surely we will die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered.”

samuel2.14.p4.b2.text: “Yet God does not take away a life; but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.”

samuel2.14.p4.b3.text: “For my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God.”

samuel2.14.p5.b1.text: “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?”

samuel2.14.p5.b2.text: “Today, … your servant knows that he has found favor with you, my lord the king …”

samuel2.14.p5.b3.text: So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

samuel2.14.p5.b4.text: “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.”

samuel2.14.p6.b1.text: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.

samuel2.14.p6.b2.text: And when he cut the hair of his head—he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy—he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.

samuel2.14.p6.b3.text: Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman.

samuel2.14.p7.b1.text: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.

samuel2.14.p7.b2.text: “… he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!”

samuel2.14.p7.b3.text: “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”

samuel2.14.p7.b4.text: “… So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”

samuel2.14.p8.b1.text: So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, …

samuel2.14.p8.b2.text: … who came to him and bowed facedown before him.
